bull_bear.body:
- Cluster-based expansion builds dense contiguous networks that improve supply chain efficiency, strengthen regional brand visibility and optimise marketing and operating costs
- Eastern India leadership with a dominant presence in West Bengal, Odisha, Assam and Bihar, which together account for 205 of 263 stores
- Private label portfolio of 11 in-house brands lifted revenue contribution from 45% in FY 2024-25 to 53% in FY 2025-26, strengthening sourcing efficiencies, pricing flexibility and margins; private labels deliver a 0.75-1.5 percentage point margin advantage over branded and third-party products
- Underpenetrated-market footprint - 45% of stores in Tier III and 25% in Tier IV cities, only 4% in metros - giving headroom for expansion into Rising Bharat catchments
- Integrated technology backbone across SAP HANA ERP, INFOR WMS, POS and a Goldratt-based demand-pull replenishment model, with all 263 stores on a unified digital backbone for real-time visibility
- Centralised Serampore warehousing with cross-docking and transport collection centres enabling faster replenishment and lower distribution cost
- Loyal customer base with a 71% repeat customer rate and 44.5 million customer footfall in FY 2025-26

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Supply chain disruption — Natural disasters, logistics challenges or operational interruptions may impact inventory availability and store operations. The risk is concrete for this business: a fire on May 20, 2024 at the erstwhile central warehouse at Serampore, West Bengal destroyed inventory and capital assets, and the model concentrates distribution in a single central warehouse. Mitigated through contingency plans, insurance coverage and business continuity measures.
- Inventory management — Inefficient inventory planning may result in overstocking, stock-outs and increased working capital requirements - material for a value fashion retailer holding 119 days of inventory. Mitigated through demand forecasting, inventory planning and store-level replenishment aligned to customer preferences and sales trends.
- Human capital - attrition and talent shortage — High employee attrition and talent shortages may impact operational efficiency, customer service and business growth. The BRSR discloses a permanent-employee turnover rate of 100% in FY 2025-26 against 17.84% in FY 2024-25, a sharp deterioration for a labour-intensive store network that grew headcount ~30% YoY. Mitigated through employee engagement, capability development, performance-based rewards and career progression.
- Geographic and market concentration — Structural concentration risk: approximately 35% of revenue is generated from West Bengal alone, 98 of 263 stores are in West Bengal and 205 of 263 stores sit in the four core markets of West Bengal, Odisha, Assam and Bihar. A single-state economic, regulatory or civil disruption is material - operations at the Dhuliyan, West Bengal store were temporarily disrupted during the year due to civil unrest.
- Single-activity concentration in value fashion retail — The BRSR reports 100% of turnover from a single business activity - retail trading of apparel and non-apparel consumer products - with apparel alone at 86% of revenue and nil exports. There is no diversification cushion if discretionary apparel demand weakens; the Cupid partnership adding personal care is the only stated diversification lever and has yet to contribute.
- Product quality and liability — Product quality issues may affect customer trust, brand reputation and expose the Company to liability claims - heightened as private labels rise to 53% of revenue and the Company owns quality accountability for those brands. Mitigated through quality assurance and control processes across the sourcing and distribution value chain.
- Financial risks - credit, liquidity, interest rate and market — Exposure to credit, liquidity, interest rate and market risks may affect financial performance and cash flows; relevant given the leased store estate and continued investment in accelerating expansion. Mitigated through prudent financial planning, adequate liquidity reserves and risk management strategies.
- Regulatory and external risks — Changes in economic conditions, regulations and the political environment may impact business operations and growth. Concretely, the four Labour Codes notified by the Government of India on November 21, 2025 already had an impact recognised in the year. Mitigated through continuous monitoring of the external environment and assessment of emerging risks.
- Business continuity — Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications; the Business Continuity Plan covers People, Facilities and Critical IT Infrastructure with periodically tested Disaster Recovery sites, and comprehensive training for retail staff, managers and leaders.
- Climate change and physical/transition exposure — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as both opportunity and risk with negative financial implications: extreme weather may disrupt operations and supply chains, affect sourcing partners and raise costs of goods; water availability may constrain the Company and its value chain partners; and transition to a low-carbon economy may bring stricter regulation and higher compliance costs. Mitigated via a market strategy matrix integrating energy and water conservation, sustainable building materials, recycling/reuse and transportation efficiency.

outlook.body:
- Cluster-based expansion: build dense retail networks across contiguous geographies to improve supply chain efficiency, strengthen brand visibility and optimise operating costs; 49 net new stores were added and 19 new cities entered in FY 2025-26.
- Deepen presence in underserved Tier 2, Tier 3 and Tier 4 markets, where nearly 70% of stores are already located, rather than in metros.
- Accelerate private label growth - expand the portfolio of exclusive brands to strengthen product differentiation, improve sourcing efficiencies and lift gross margins, targeting 65% of revenue by FY 2026-27 from 53% in FY 2025-26.
- Maintain private label MRPs largely unchanged under an 'attractive pricing' regime, transitioning to 'fair pricing' only once brand equity is established; keep private label participation in General Merchandise intentionally limited to Home Focus and partially Miss19, since that category's strategic role is driving footfalls.
- Broaden the lifestyle proposition beyond fashion via the Cupid Limited partnership, adding personal care and wellness to General Merchandise while keeping the Apparel-General Merchandise revenue mix broadly stable.
- Expand the family-focused value proposition as a one-stop destination spanning apparel, home essentials, beauty, toys and stationery with regionally relevant, affordably priced assortments.
- Drive operational excellence through technology - SAP S/4HANA (implemented via greenfield deployment in FY 2025-26), INFOR WMS, POS, DOMO data warehousing and analytics, PeopleStrong HRMS, and a planned Transportation Management System.
- Optimise inventory and supply chain efficiency through demand-led planning, the Automatic Replenishment System and a Goldratt-based demand-pull replenishment model with structured markdown management.
- Enhance store productivity through disciplined store planning, category optimisation and customer-centric merchandising, maximising returns per square foot.
- Build omni-channel reach through Endless Aisle, AI-enabled personalised marketing, CRM engagement across SMS, WhatsApp and email, and a creator ecosystem.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Baazar Style Retail's expansion is store-led and cluster-based rather than manufacturing capex; the BRSR confirms the Company operates through retail outlets and is not engaged in any manufacturing activity. During FY 2025-26 the network grew to 263 stores across 191 cities in 9 states from 214 stores a year earlier - a net addition of 49 stores (the Chairman/MD letter states 56 new stores were opened while 7 were rationalised), with 19 new cities entered (the MD's letter separately states 22 new cities). Total retail space expanded from approximately 19.21 lakh sq. ft. in FY 2024-25 to 24.58 lakh sq. ft. in FY 2025-26 (approximately 2.5 million sq. ft.), with average store size up 4% to 9,345 sq. ft. The core markets of West Bengal, Odisha, Assam and Bihar account for 205 stores and the focus markets of Jharkhand, Andhra Pradesh, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh and Arunachal Pradesh a further 58; state-wise store counts moved over FY24-FY26 as West Bengal 62/77/98, Odisha 28/34/35, Assam 25/34/38, Bihar 17/26/34, Jharkhand 9/14/16, Andhra Pradesh 6/5/5, Tripura 2/2/3, Uttar Pradesh 12/21/33 and Arunachal Pradesh nil/1/1. Supply chain capacity was expanded alongside: the central warehouse at Serampore, West Bengal now spans approximately 3.25 lakh sq. ft. as of the date of the Annual Report (described elsewhere as approximately 400,000 sq. ft. and as 3 sheds of about 300,000 sq. ft.), with 5,000 pallet positions of cross-dock capacity, four transport collection centres of about 15,000 sq. ft. each across four states (three added during FY 2025-26), and throughput of about 400,000 inbound and 400,000 outbound pieces per day. Technology build-out during the year included a greenfield SAP S/4HANA deployment integrating WMS, POS, Vendor Portal, TMS, Merchandise Planning, Banking and Data Warehouse; DOMO as the unified data warehousing and analytics platform; and the initiation of PeopleStrong HRMS, with a Transportation Management System implementation planned. Category expansion is being pursued through a strategic partnership with Cupid Limited, supported by its Rs 3,315.30 Mn investment, to add personal care and wellness to General Merchandise. A proposed equity issue is referenced whose objects include capital expenditure for opening of new stores and general corporate purposes, but the bundle text is truncated before the instrument, size or timeline can be read.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Organised retail formalisation: Indian retail is shifting from small family-owned shops towards supermarkets, hypermarkets and large chains, supported by liberalised FDI norms, rising disposable incomes and an expanding middle class seeking branded merchandise and quality assurance.
- Tier II and Tier III cities emerging as growth engines, with over 60% of India's e-commerce transactions now originating from those cities - directly aligned with the Company's underpenetrated-market footprint.
- India's apparel market, estimated at Rs 9.3 lakh crore in FY 2024-25, has grown at a ~7% CAGR since FY 2017-18 and is projected to reach Rs 16 lakh crore by FY 2029-30, with organised players holding ~41% of the market.
- India retail market projected to expand from USD 1,124.2 billion in 2025 to USD 3,505.4 billion by 2034 at a 12.80% CAGR, driven by rising disposable income, urbanisation and digital adoption.
- Gen Z is expected to account for 43% of India's total consumption in 2025 with an estimated US$250 billion in direct spending power, fuelling demand for fashion and personal care.
- Retail growth accelerating across East and Central India, supported by improving infrastructure, digital connectivity, rising incomes and stronger supply chain networks - the Company's core geography.
- Margin lever from private label penetration: private labels deliver a 0.75-1.5 percentage point margin advantage over branded and third-party products, and General Merchandise carries gross margins of approximately 32-33%.
- Operating leverage from scale: EBITDA margin expanded by 27 basis points to 14.3% from 14.1% despite continued investment in accelerating store expansion.
- Store portfolio maturity: a substantial portion of the store portfolio remained in the ramp-up stage, implying headroom in productivity as stores season.
- Working capital lever: inventory holding days improved to 119 from 129 and inventory turnover rose to 2.04x from 1.87x.
- Management notes changing consumer behaviour as the principal challenge for retailers, alongside competitive pressure, logistics and supply chain infrastructure bottlenecks and shifting regulatory policies.
- Macro backdrop: India's real GDP is projected to grow 6.80-7.20% in FY 2026-27 with retail inflation within the RBI target range, supporting consumption.

currentContext.expansion: Baazar Style Retail's expansion is store-led and cluster-based rather than manufacturing capex; the BRSR confirms the Company operates through retail outlets and is not engaged in any manufacturing activity. During FY 2025-26 the network grew to 263 stores across 191 cities in 9 states from 214 stores a year earlier - a net addition of 49 stores (the Chairman/MD letter states 56 new stores were opened while 7 were rationalised), with 19 new cities entered (the MD's letter separately states 22 new cities). Total retail space expanded from approximately 19.21 lakh sq. ft. in FY 2024-25 to 24.58 lakh sq. ft. in FY 2025-26 (approximately 2.5 million sq. ft.), with average store size up 4% to 9,345 sq. ft. The core markets of West Bengal, Odisha, Assam and Bihar account for 205 stores and the focus markets of Jharkhand, Andhra Pradesh, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh and Arunachal Pradesh a further 58; state-wise store counts moved over FY24-FY26 as West Bengal 62/77/98, Odisha 28/34/35, Assam 25/34/38, Bihar 17/26/34, Jharkhand 9/14/16, Andhra Pradesh 6/5/5, Tripura 2/2/3, Uttar Pradesh 12/21/33 and Arunachal Pradesh nil/1/1. Supply chain capacity was expanded alongside: the central warehouse at Serampore, West Bengal now spans approximately 3.25 lakh sq. ft. as of the date of the Annual Report (described elsewhere as approximately 400,000 sq. ft. and as 3 sheds of about 300,000 sq. ft.), with 5,000 pallet positions of cross-dock capacity, four transport collection centres of about 15,000 sq. ft. each across four states (three added during FY 2025-26), and throughput of about 400,000 inbound and 400,000 outbound pieces per day. Technology build-out during the year included a greenfield SAP S/4HANA deployment integrating WMS, POS, Vendor Portal, TMS, Merchandise Planning, Banking and Data Warehouse; DOMO as the unified data warehousing and analytics platform; and the initiation of PeopleStrong HRMS, with a Transportation Management System implementation planned. Category expansion is being pursued through a strategic partnership with Cupid Limited, supported by its Rs 3,315.30 Mn investment, to add personal care and wellness to General Merchandise. risks.note: Natural disasters, logistics challenges or operational interruptions may impact inventory availability and store operations. The risk is concrete for this business: a fire on May 20, 2024 at the erstwhile central warehouse at Serampore, West Bengal destroyed inventory and capital assets, and the model concentrates distribution in a single central warehouse. Mitigated through contingency plans, insurance coverage and business continuity measures.

Inefficient inventory planning may result in overstocking, stock-outs and increased working capital requirements - material for a value fashion retailer holding 119 days of inventory. Mitigated through demand forecasting, inventory planning and store-level replenishment aligned to customer preferences and sales trends.

risks.risk: Human capital - attrition and talent shortage
risks.note: High employee attrition and talent shortages may impact operational efficiency, customer service and business growth. The BRSR discloses a permanent-employee turnover rate of 100% in FY 2025-26 against 17.84% in FY 2024-25, a sharp deterioration for a labour-intensive store network that grew headcount ~30% YoY. Mitigated through employee engagement, capability development, performance-based rewards and career progression.

Structural concentration risk: approximately 35% of revenue is generated from West Bengal alone, 98 of 263 stores are in West Bengal and 205 of 263 stores sit in the four core markets of West Bengal, Odisha, Assam and Bihar. A single-state economic, regulatory or civil disruption is material - operations at the Dhuliyan, West Bengal store were temporarily disrupted during the year due to civil unrest.

risks.risk: Single-activity concentration in value fashion retail
risks.note: The BRSR reports 100% of turnover from a single business activity - retail trading of apparel and non-apparel consumer products - with apparel alone at 86% of revenue and nil exports. There is no diversification cushion if discretionary apparel demand weakens; the Cupid partnership adding personal care is the only stated diversification lever and has yet to contribute.

Product quality issues may affect customer trust, brand reputation and expose the Company to liability claims - heightened as private labels rise to 53% of revenue and the Company owns quality accountability for those brands. Mitigated through quality assurance and control processes across the sourcing and distribution value chain.

risks.risk: Financial risks - credit, liquidity, interest rate and market
risks.note: Exposure to credit, liquidity, interest rate and market risks may affect financial performance and cash flows; relevant given the leased store estate and continued investment in accelerating expansion. Mitigated through prudent financial planning, adequate liquidity reserves and risk management strategies.

Changes in economic conditions, regulations and the political environment may impact business operations and growth. Concretely, the four Labour Codes notified by the Government of India on November 21, 2025 already had an impact recognised in the year. Mitigated through continuous monitoring of the external environment and assessment of emerging risks.

Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications; the Business Continuity Plan covers People, Facilities and Critical IT Infrastructure with periodically tested Disaster Recovery sites, and comprehensive training for retail staff, managers and leaders.

Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as both opportunity and risk with negative financial implications: extreme weather may disrupt operations and supply chains, affect sourcing partners and raise costs of goods; water availability may constrain the Company and its value chain partners; and transition to a low-carbon economy may bring stricter regulation and higher compliance costs. Mitigated via a market strategy matrix integrating energy and water conservation, sustainable building materials, recycling/reuse and transportation efficiency.

demand_drivers.body:
- Organised retail formalisation: Indian retail is shifting from small family-owned shops towards supermarkets, hypermarkets and large chains, supported by liberalised FDI norms, rising disposable incomes and an expanding middle class seeking branded merchandise and quality assurance.
- Tier II and Tier III cities emerging as growth engines, with over 60% of India's e-commerce transactions now originating from those cities - directly aligned with the Company's underpenetrated-market footprint.
- India's apparel market, estimated at Rs 9.3 lakh crore in FY 2024-25, has grown at a ~7% CAGR since FY 2017-18 and is projected to reach Rs 16 lakh crore by FY 2029-30, with organised players holding ~41% of the market.
- India retail market projected to expand from USD 1,124.2 billion in 2025 to USD 3,505.4 billion by 2034 at a 12.80% CAGR, driven by rising disposable income, urbanisation and digital adoption.
- Gen Z is expected to account for 43% of India's total consumption in 2025 with an estimated US$250 billion in direct spending power, fuelling demand for fashion and personal care.
- Retail growth accelerating across East and Central India, supported by improving infrastructure, digital connectivity, rising incomes and stronger supply chain networks - the Company's core geography.
- Margin lever from private label penetration: private labels deliver a 0.75-1.5 percentage point margin advantage over branded and third-party products, and General Merchandise carries gross margins of approximately 32-33%.
- Operating leverage from scale: EBITDA margin expanded by 27 basis points to 14.3% from 14.1% despite continued investment in accelerating store expansion.
- Store portfolio maturity: a substantial portion of the store portfolio remained in the ramp-up stage, implying headroom in productivity as stores season.
- Working capital lever: inventory holding days improved to 119 from 129 and inventory turnover rose to 2.04x from 1.87x.
- Management notes changing consumer behaviour as the principal challenge for retailers, alongside competitive pressure, logistics and supply chain infrastructure bottlenecks and shifting regulatory policies.
- Macro backdrop: India's real GDP is projected to grow 6.80-7.20% in FY 2026-27 with retail inflation within the RBI target range, supporting consumption.

capex_expansion.body: Baazar Style Retail's expansion is store-led and cluster-based rather than manufacturing capex; the BRSR confirms the Company operates through retail outlets and is not engaged in any manufacturing activity. During FY 2025-26 the network grew to 263 stores across 191 cities in 9 states from 214 stores a year earlier - a net addition of 49 stores (the Chairman/MD letter states 56 new stores were opened while 7 were rationalised), with 19 new cities entered (the MD's letter separately states 22 new cities). Total retail space expanded from approximately 19.21 lakh sq. ft. in FY 2024-25 to 24.58 lakh sq. ft. in FY 2025-26 (approximately 2.5 million sq. ft.), with average store size up 4% to 9,345 sq. ft. The core markets of West Bengal, Odisha, Assam and Bihar account for 205 stores and the focus markets of Jharkhand, Andhra Pradesh, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh and Arunachal Pradesh a further 58; state-wise store counts moved over FY24-FY26 as West Bengal 62/77/98, Odisha 28/34/35, Assam 25/34/38, Bihar 17/26/34, Jharkhand 9/14/16, Andhra Pradesh 6/5/5, Tripura 2/2/3, Uttar Pradesh 12/21/33 and Arunachal Pradesh nil/1/1. Supply chain capacity was expanded alongside: the central warehouse at Serampore, West Bengal now spans approximately 3.25 lakh sq. ft. as of the date of the Annual Report (described elsewhere as approximately 400,000 sq. ft. and as 3 sheds of about 300,000 sq. ft.), with 5,000 pallet positions of cross-dock capacity, four transport collection centres of about 15,000 sq. ft. each across four states (three added during FY 2025-26), and throughput of about 400,000 inbound and 400,000 outbound pieces per day. Technology build-out during the year included a greenfield SAP S/4HANA deployment integrating WMS, POS, Vendor Portal, TMS, Merchandise Planning, Banking and Data Warehouse; DOMO as the unified data warehousing and analytics platform; and the initiation of PeopleStrong HRMS, with a Transportation Management System implementation planned. Category expansion is being pursued through a strategic partnership with Cupid Limited, supported by its Rs 3,315.30 Mn investment, to add personal care and wellness to General Merchandise. A proposed equity issue is referenced whose objects include capital expenditure for opening of new stores and general corporate purposes, but the bundle text is truncated before the instrument, size or timeline can be read.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Cluster-based expansion builds dense contiguous networks that improve supply chain efficiency, strengthen regional brand visibility and optimise marketing and operating costs
- Eastern India leadership with a dominant presence in West Bengal, Odisha, Assam and Bihar, which together account for 205 of 263 stores
- Private label portfolio of 11 in-house brands lifted revenue contribution from 45% in FY 2024-25 to 53% in FY 2025-26, strengthening sourcing efficiencies, pricing flexibility and margins; private labels deliver a 0.75-1.5 percentage point margin advantage over branded and third-party products
- Underpenetrated-market footprint - 45% of stores in Tier III and 25% in Tier IV cities, only 4% in metros - giving headroom for expansion into Rising Bharat catchments
- Integrated technology backbone across SAP HANA ERP, INFOR WMS, POS and a Goldratt-based demand-pull replenishment model, with all 263 stores on a unified digital backbone for real-time visibility
- Centralised Serampore warehousing with cross-docking and transport collection centres enabling faster replenishment and lower distribution cost
- Loyal customer base with a 71% repeat customer rate and 44.5 million customer footfall in FY 2025-26
- One-stop family destination proposition spanning apparel plus general merchandise, encouraging cross-shopping and larger baskets

themes.title: Quick-commerce, omnichannel & retail expansion
themes.need: Quick-commerce and value retail are the structural growth engine, and Q1FY27 rewrote the unit-economics model. ETERNAL raised Blinkit's steady-state margin from a 5-6% range to ~6% and set a first-ever 4% GAAP EBIT margin target (after ESOP and depreciation) while capex per store went from INR 1cr to INR 2.5cr (+150%) with NOV/store/day up only 60% and net working capital improving 18 to 14 days - so margin can now drift DOWN while ROCE improves. Growth also decoupled from spend: Blinkit orders +21% QoQ with MTUs above 30mn achieved on LOWER marketing spend and fewer store adds, and management called Q1 the peak of competitive intensity to date. VMM did INR 3,727cr (+18.7%) on 10% SSSG with gross margin up to 28.7% driven by lower promotional spend rather than price hikes, validated a small-format store at the same revenue/sq ft and 'pretty much the same' ROCE as large format (a ~3,000-store national opportunity), and found 20% of its quick-commerce customers had never shopped a Vishal store. SHOPERSTOP swung PAT positive (+INR 5cr vs -INR 4cr) and raised FY27 LFL guidance from 5% to ~6%; ARVINDFASN lifted gross margin 90bps to 56.7% on full-price sell-through with direct channels now 62% of sales; MEESHO cut cost per delivered order ~INR 1 QoQ despite the May fuel hike. DMART/V2RETAIL/PATELRMART on value retail; TRENT-tier branded retail via ABFRL/METROBRAND/BATAINDIA/REDTAPE.
themes.driver: Blinkit dark-store rollout at the new INR 2.5cr/store capex against the 4% GAAP EBIT target; VMM small-format expansion; festive/quick-commerce GMV. Watch ARVINDFASN's SS27 sourcing lock (next 45-60 days) - if war-inflated input costs hold, apparel pricing corrects.
